t: A frontier march east of the Elbe founded by Albert the Bear in 1157, whose ruler became one of the seven electors of the Empire.
From 1415 the Hohenzollerns ruled it, gaining Prussia in 1618 and building a standing army under the Great Elector.
In 1701 its elector became King in Prussia, and Brandenburg remained the Prussian heartland until the Empire ended in 1806.
dyk: Brandenburg had an African colony: from 1683 its fort of Gross Friedrichsburg stood on the Gold Coast in today’s Ghana, until the Prussian king sold it to the Dutch in 1717.
ev: Albert the Bear recaptures Brandenburg an der Havel and styles himself margrave
The Golden Bull confirms the margrave as an elector of the Empire
Frederick of Hohenzollern is granted the Mark and the electoral title
Joachim II introduces the Lutheran Reformation
The electors inherit the Duchy of Prussia
The Great Elector defeats the Swedes at the Battle of Fehrbellin
The Edict of Potsdam invites Huguenot refugees
Elector Frederick III crowns himself King in Prussia

f.capital: Brandenburg an der Havel; Berlin from the late 15th century
f.predecessor: Northern March; Principality of the Hevelli
